searchText: Is there any method other than using CREATE2 and then DELEGATECALL to execute arbitrary opcode from calldata within a given contract? Ordinary CREATE works, but that is not a pattern that I think fits into most smart contract mold (immutable predictable execution). For EOF that pattern will require CREATE4. Be kind and SELFDESTRUCT at the end of the contract. My goal is to have a contract which verifies a GROTH16 proof of a commitment to arbitrary bytecode, checks that the subsequent calldata matches the commitment, and then delegates into it. I thought that SELFDESTRUCT was deprecated? SELFDESTRUCT is deprecated since Shapella: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-6049 https://blog.ethereum.org/2023/03/28/shapella-mainnet-announcement Probably more this: https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/eip-6780-deactivate-selfdestruct-except-where-it-occurs-in-the-same-transaction-in-which-a-contract-was-created/13539 (Planned for Dencun) Yes, EIP-6780 is what I was alluding to with cleanup.
